newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Gaullists bury hatchet between factions.
newsitem.headline: France Gaullists bury hatchet between factions.

text.p: Philippe Seguin, new head of France's Rally for the Republic Gaullist party, announced a new RPR leadership structure on Thursday which included former Budget Minister Nicolas Sarkozy.

Sarkozy was a main force in 1995 behind the presidential candidacy of then Prime Minister Eduard Balladur who stood against fellow Gaullist Jacques Chirac, splitting the RPR into rival camps. His inclusion in the new party leadership appeared aimed at ending the feud, specialists said.

Sarkozy was among 10 people appointed to back Seguin who was elected party president on Sunday, replacing former Prime Minister Alain Juppe who was forced out because of his role in the centre-right's stunning general election defeat on June 1.
President Jacques Chirac, who now remains in office having to share power uncomfortably with a left-wing cabinet, was widely reported to have wanted Sarkozy kept out of the RPR leadership altogether.

It was not immediately clear if Chirac had finally agreed to allow Sarkozy a role in order to close party ranks or if Seguin, who is himself on cool terms with Chirac, had ignored the president's wishes.

Like Seguin, the 42-year-old Sarkozy is reported to harbour his own presidential ambitions and including him in the leadership might be a way for Seguin to keep an eye on a possible rival. The next presidential election is in 2002 and many specialists have said Chirac's now-weakened position might make it difficult for him to make a bid for his own succession.
